FIRST LEAD: Player A (seat 1) leads first in deals 1 and 3. Player B (seat 2) leads first in deals 2 and 4. After that, the winner of each trick leads the next one.

A TRICK:
(1) The leader plays any card face up. Its rank is the led rank.
(2) The follower plays any card face up. If it matches the led rank or is a Seven, the follower is currently winning. Otherwise the leader wins the trick and it ends.

(4) If the leader extended, the follower must play a second card (any card). If it matches the led rank or is a Seven, the follower wins the trick. Otherwise the leader wins.
A trick can never be extended more than 1 time.

Both players always play the same number of cards, so both hands empty together. - **They follow with their Ace:** the rest of the deal splits 30–30.

FIRST LEAD: Player A (seat 1) leads first in deals 1 and 3. Player B (seat 2) leads first in deals 2 and 4. After that, the winner of each trick leads the next one.

A TRICK:

(2) The follower plays any card face up. If it matches the led rank or is a Seven, the follower is currently winning. Otherwise the leader wins the trick and it ends.

(4) If the leader extended, the follower must play a second card (any card). If it matches the led rank or is a Seven, the follower wins the trick. Otherwise the leader wins.
A trick can never be extended more than 1 time.

AFTER EACH TRICK: all cards played in the trick are announced. The winner scores 10 points for each Ace and each Ten among them. Both players always play the same number of cards, so both hands empty together. If the hands are now empty, the winner of this trick also scores 10 points for the last trick, and the deal ends; any remaining rounds of that deal are skipped. A deal lasts 4 to 8 tricks.

INFORMATION: each player sees their own hand and every card played. Neither sees the opponent's hand or the set-aside cards.

[user]
=== Sedmice Duel ===

Sedmice Duel is played with 32 cards: 4 each of the ranks 7, 8, 9, 10, J, Q, K, A. Suits do not matter. Aces and Tens are point cards worth 10 each. Sevens are wild. Seat 1 is Player A and seat 2 is Player B.

The match is 4 deals. Each deal lasts up to 8 rounds, so the match has 32 rounds; each round is one trick.

DEALING (first round of each deal): the full deck is shuffled. Each player receives exactly one Seven, one Ace and one Ten, then 5 more random cards from the remaining 26, so each hand has 8 cards. Hands are private. The 16 undealt cards are set aside face down and are never revealed or used in that deal.

FIRST LEAD: Player A (seat 1) leads first in deals 1 and 3. Player B (seat 2) leads first in deals 2 and 4. After that, the winner of each trick leads the next one.

A TRICK:
(1) The leader plays any card face up. Its rank is the led rank.
(2) The follower plays any card face up. If it matches the led rank or is a Seven, the follower is currently winning. Otherwise the leader wins the trick and it ends.
(3) If the follower is currently winning, the leader may extend once by playing a second card that matches the led rank or is a Seven. The leader may also decline. If the leader declines or has no such card, the follower wins the trick.
(4) If the leader extended, the follower must play a second card (any card). If it matches the led rank or is a Seven, the follower wins the trick. Otherwise the leader wins.
A trick can never be extended more than 1 time.

AFTER EACH TRICK: all cards played in the trick are announced. The winner scores 10 points for each Ace and each Ten among them. Both players always play the same number of cards, so both hands empty together. If the hands are now empty, the winner of this trick also scores 10 points for the last trick, and the deal ends; any remaining rounds of that deal are skipped. A deal lasts 4 to 8 tricks.

INFORMATION: each player sees their own hand and every card played. Neither sees the opponent's hand or the set-aside cards.

After 4 deals, the player with the higher total points wins. Equal totals are a draw (a shared win).

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 2. Seats are numbered 1 to 2.
You are seat 2, Blaise. Seats are referred to by number.

Seat 1 is Player A and seat 2 is Player B.
The dealing rule: each deal, each hand gets exactly one Seven, one Ace and one Ten, plus 5 random cards from the remaining 26, for 8 cards. The other 16 cards are set aside face down and never used that deal.

  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,

  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

records.prompt:
[user]
=== Sedmice Duel ===

Sedmice Duel is played with 32 cards: 4 each of the ranks 7, 8, 9, 10, J, Q, K, A. Suits do not matter. Aces and Tens are point cards worth 10 each. Sevens are wild. Seat 1 is Player A and seat 2 is Player B.

The match is 4 deals. Each deal lasts up to 8 rounds, so the match has 32 rounds; each round is one trick.

DEALING (first round of each deal): the full deck is shuffled. Each player receives exactly one Seven, one Ace and one Ten, then 5 more random cards from the remaining 26, so each hand has 8 cards. Hands are private. The 16 undealt cards are set aside face down and are never revealed or used in that deal.

FIRST LEAD: Player A (seat 1) leads first in deals 1 and 3. Player B (seat 2) leads first in deals 2 and 4. After that, the winner of each trick leads the next one.

A TRICK:
(1) The leader plays any card face up. Its rank is the led rank.
(2) The follower plays any card face up. If it matches the led rank or is a Seven, the follower is currently winning. Otherwise the leader wins the trick and it ends.
(3) If the follower is currently winning, the leader may extend once by playing a second card that matches the led rank or is a Seven. The leader may also decline. If the leader declines or has no such card, the follower wins the trick.
(4) If the leader extended, the follower must play a second card (any card). If it matches the led rank or is a Seven, the follower wins the trick. Otherwise the leader wins.
A trick can never be extended more than 1 time.

AFTER EACH TRICK: all cards played in the trick are announced. The winner scores 10 points for each Ace and each Ten among them. Both players always play the same number of cards, so both hands empty together. If the hands are now empty, the winner of this trick also scores 10 points for the last trick, and the deal ends; any remaining rounds of that deal are skipped. A deal lasts 4 to 8 tricks.

INFORMATION: each player sees their own hand and every card played. Neither sees the opponent's hand or the set-aside cards.

After 4 deals, the player with the higher total points wins. Equal totals are a draw (a shared win).

--- Your place at the table ---

Players: 2. Seats are numbered 1 to 2.
You are seat 1, Ada. Seats are referred to by number.

What you know to begin with:

Seat 1 is Player A and seat 2 is Player B.
The dealing rule: each deal, each hand gets exactly one Seven, one Ace and one Ten, plus 5 random cards from the remaining 26, for 8 cards. The other 16 cards are set aside face down and never used that deal.

Each round runs in this order: the deal → your hand → leader's first card → follower's first card → leader's extension → follower's second card → the trick is won → after the trick → reset the trick → after the last deal.

Actions you may be asked for:
  leader's_first_card answer with one of the options you are given
  follower's_first_card answer with one of the options you are given
  leader's_extension answer with one of the options you are given

How we will talk, for the rest of the match:

  GAME_START       This message. Sent once, before the first round.
  SITUATION        Something happened that you are allowed to know.
                   Do not reply. Wait to be asked.
  YOUR_TURN        Your turn to act. Reply with exactly one action,
                   in the format the message states.
  ACTION_REJECTED  Your last answer was not legal. Answer again.
  GAME_END         The match is over.

You will only ever be told what you are entitled to know. Other seats are told
different things. Nothing reaches you except through these messages.

FIRST LEAD: Player A (seat 1) leads first in deals 1 and 3. Player B (seat 2) leads first in deals 2 and 4. After that, the winner of each trick leads the next one.

records.system:
You are reviewing a game that has finished. You were not a player. You are shown everything: the messages the table was told, every move, and each player's private thinking at every move, which no other player ever saw. Each move carries the notes its game asked for, under their own names. The usual ones are:

  plan     what they meant to do over the coming turns
  reason   why they made that move
  predict  what they expected their opponents to do
  adjust   how they changed their own strategy because of that

Write two things.

First, a summary of the whole game as it unfolded: the turning points, the moves that decided it, and how it ended. Concrete: name seats, rounds and numbers.

Second, a review of each player. Judge their play, not their luck. For each one, compare their predictions with what their opponents were actually thinking and actually did: were they right, and did they see it in time? Did their adjustments follow from their predictions, and did their moves follow from their reasons? Point out their best and worst moves. Then score their play from 1 to 10, where 1 is aimless or self-defeating and 10 is sharp, well read and well executed. A player can lose and still score well, or win and score badly.

A player who gave no reasons, predictions or adjustments is judged on their moves alone; say that their thinking was not recorded.

Refer to each player by seat, and as "they".

THE GAME
Sedmice Duel is played with 32 cards: 4 each of the ranks 7, 8, 9, 10, J, Q, K, A. Suits do not matter. Aces and Tens are point cards worth 10 each. Sevens are wild. Seat 1 is Player A and seat 2 is Player B.

The match is 4 deals. Each deal lasts up to 8 rounds, so the match has 32 rounds; each round is one trick.

DEALING (first round of each deal): the full deck is shuffled. Each player receives exactly one Seven, one Ace and one Ten, then 5 more random cards from the remaining 26, so each hand has 8 cards. Hands are private. The 16 undealt cards are set aside face down and are never revealed or used in that deal.

FIRST LEAD: Player A (seat 1) leads first in deals 1 and 3. Player B (seat 2) leads first in deals 2 and 4. After that, the winner of each trick leads the next one.

A TRICK:
(1) The leader plays any card face up. Its rank is the led rank.
(2) The follower plays any card face up. If it matches the led rank or is a Seven, the follower is currently winning. Otherwise the leader wins the trick and it ends.
(3) If the follower is currently winning, the leader may extend once by playing a second card that matches the led rank or is a Seven. The leader may also decline. If the leader declines or has no such card, the follower wins the trick.
(4) If the leader extended, the follower must play a second card (any card). If it matches the led rank or is a Seven, the follower wins the trick. Otherwise the leader wins.
A trick can never be extended more than 1 time.

AFTER EACH TRICK: all cards played in the trick are announced. The winner scores 10 points for each Ace and each Ten among them. Both players always play the same number of cards, so both hands empty together. If the hands are now empty, the winner of this trick also scores 10 points for the last trick, and the deal ends; any remaining rounds of that deal are skipped. A deal lasts 4 to 8 tricks.

INFORMATION: each player sees their own hand and every card played. Neither sees the opponent's hand or the set-aside cards.

After 4 deals, the player with the higher total points wins. Equal totals are a draw (a shared win).
